p1-01.claim: You don’t have a discipline problem. You have a self-trust problem.

p1-02.definition: The evidence you’ve collected that you do what you say. Every promise to yourself you break is a vote against you.

p1-03.quote: Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running.
p1-03.note: Trust works the same way. You build it by keeping promises, not by making bigger ones.

p1-04.title: Shrink the promise
p1-04.body: Pick one you can’t fail: ten push-ups, one page, in bed by 23:30.

p1-05.title: Keep it for 7 days
p1-05.body: Not 30. Seven. Then raise it by one notch.

p1-06.title: Count the proof
p1-06.body: Tick a box every night. You’re not tracking a habit. You’re collecting evidence about who you are.

p1-07.line: Small promises, kept, become a self you can trust.
p1-07.action: Save this. Send it to the friend who keeps starting on Monday.

p2-01.claim: When someone is rude to you today, Marcus Aurelius had already planned for it.

p2-02.quote: Begin the morning by saying to yourself: I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
p2-02.note: He wasn’t being bitter. He was getting ready.

rows: Someone cuts you off in traffic
Your boss snaps in a meeting
Already on today's list. Scroll on.

p2-04.quote: Take away your opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, ‘I have been harmed.’ Take away the complaint, ‘I have been harmed,’ and the harm is taken away.
p2-04.note: Rude happened. Harmed is a story you can decline.

p2-05.title: Say it before you leave the house
p2-05.body: “Someone will be rude to me today. It won’t be about me.” Ten seconds. Then go.

p2-06.line: You can’t control their mood. You can be ready for it.
p2-06.action: Send this to someone who deals with people all day.

p3-01.claim: Why you replay the argument at 2am

p3-02.definition: Replaying a problem without moving it forward. At night nothing competes for your attention, so the loop gets louder.

p3-03.quote: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
p3-03.note: The argument lasted five minutes. The replay lasts three hours.

p3-04.quote: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
p3-04.note: You’re not replaying what happened. You’re replaying what you decided it meant.

p3-05.title: Write the judgment down
p3-05.body: One line: “It means I’m ___.” On paper, a feeling becomes a claim you can check.

p3-06.title: Is it true? Is it mine to fix?
p3-06.body: True and yours: set one action for tomorrow. Neither: it’s finished. Put the pen down.

p3-07.line: The loop ends when you look at the judgment, not when you win the argument.

p4-01.claim: The 5-minute evening review the Stoics actually ran
p4-01.sub: Seneca did it every night. Here is the routine.

p4-02.quote: I scan the whole of my day and retrace all my deeds and words. I conceal nothing from myself, I omit nothing.

p4-03.definition: Look at everything. Punish nothing. You’re collecting notes for tomorrow, not building a case against yourself.

p4-04.title: Set the scene
p4-04.body: Same time, same place, lights low. Phone in another room. Notebook open.

p4-05.title: Replay the day in order
p4-05.body: Morning to night, like watching footage. Don’t skip the parts you’d rather not see.

p4-06.title: “What bad habit have you cured today?”
p4-06.body: Seneca’s first question. One small win counts.

p4-07.title: “What fault have you resisted?”
p4-07.body: The angry text you didn’t send. The scroll you stopped.

p4-08.title: “In what respect are you better?”
p4-08.body: Compare yourself with yesterday’s you. Nobody else.

p4-09.title: Pick one thing for tomorrow
p4-09.body: One sentence. Not a plan. A direction.

p4-10.line: Five minutes. Every night. Honest, not harsh.
p4-10.action: Save this, do it tonight, and tell me which question was hardest.
